cards.title: 新加速牛顿法实现O(1/k^3)全局收敛率，仅需单次线性求解

entities.name: 牛顿法
entities.explain: 一种经典的优化算法，利用函数的二阶导数信息来快速找到最小值点

entities.name: Lipschitz连续Hessian
entities.explain: 一种数学条件，保证函数的二阶导数变化不会过于剧烈，是算法分析中的常见假设

cards.summary: 研究者提出一种新的直接加速牛顿法，用于最小化具有Lipschitz连续Hessian的凸函数。该算法仅使用原始变量，每次迭代只需一次线性求解，通过简单的预定参数选择，实现了O(1/k^3)的全局收敛率。这是该问题类别中首个仅依赖单次线性求解就达到此收敛率的二阶方法。
cards.relevant: 该成果在优化算法领域具有理论突破意义，为大规模机器学习模型训练提供了更高效的二阶优化工具。
cards.source_text: Primal Acceleration of Newton's Method。We develop a new direct accelerated Newton method for minimizing convex functions with Lipschitz continuous Hessian. The algorithm uses only primal variables and performs just one linear solve per iteration. With a simple predetermined choice of parameters, it achieves the global convergence rate of $O(1/k^3)$ in terms of the functional residual. entities.name: VIALS

entities.name: 视觉问答
entities.explain: 一种AI任务，模型需要根据图像内容回答自然语言问题

cards.summary: VIALS是一个针对生命科学工作流程的视觉问答基准，包含161个解读任务，涵盖凝胶印迹、显微镜图像、质粒图谱等专业工件。与现有基准不同，VIALS聚焦于生物技术行业实验流程中的实际工件，而非出版物中的精美图表。该基准旨在评估前沿视觉语言模型在专业场景下的表现。
cards.relevant: 该基准填补了生命科学领域AI视觉解读评估的空白，对推动AI在生物技术研发中的应用具有重要意义。

cards.title: 生成式AI颠覆机器验证：一人可安全指挥AI代理舰队

entities.name: 机器验证
entities.explain: 通过自动化工具证明软件或硬件系统正确性的过程，传统上成本高昂

entities.name: AI代理
entities.explain: 能够自主执行任务的人工智能程序，可独立完成从编码到验证的多个步骤

cards.summary: 研究者报告称，生成式AI彻底改变了机器验证的成本结构：在AI速度下，验证不仅经济可行，而且对生产力至关重要。在五周内，一名研究人员通过消费级AI订阅，指挥一小队AI代理从应用代码到验证的完整流程，展示了AI作为不可腐蚀的裁判，使单人安全地指挥大规模自主机器工作成为可能。
cards.relevant: 该成果可能彻底改变软件开发和验证的范式，大幅降低验证成本，提高AI代理系统的可靠性和安全性。

cards.relevant: 该框架直接回应了ASR系统在生产环境中的实际需求，对提升语音助手、会议转录等应用的用户体验有直接价值。

entities.explain: 一种将解剖学知识作为约束条件嵌入深度学习模型的新方法

entities.name: SE(3)
entities.explain: 三维空间中的特殊欧几里得群，描述物体的旋转和平移变换

cards.title: PerturbRx：学习治疗条件下的潜在转换以预测患者药物反应

entities.name: PerturbRx
entities.explain: 一种治疗条件化的表示学习框架，用于预测癌症患者的药物反应

entities.name: 肿瘤异质性
entities.explain: 不同肿瘤细胞或不同患者之间在分子和表型上的差异，是癌症治疗困难的原因之一

cards.summary: PerturbRx提出一种治疗条件化的表示学习框架，通过学习干预诱导的潜在状态转换来预测患者对药物的反应。该框架训练药物和剂量条件化的转换模型，将预处理分子谱和药物表征结合，显式建模治疗下的分子变化。这一方法有望改善癌症治疗反应预测的准确性。
cards.relevant: 该研究针对癌症治疗中的个性化用药需求，通过建模治疗引起的分子变化，为精准医疗提供了新的预测工具。

Existing approaches predict response from pretreatment molecular profiles and drug representations, without explicitly modeling the molecular changes expected under treatment. We propose PerturbRx, a treatment-conditioned representation learning framework that learns intervention-induced latent transitions and uses them as patient-drug response features. cards.source_title: PerturbRx: Learning Treatment-Conditioned Latent Transitions for Patient Drug Response Prediction

cards.title: 研究证明：顺序预测中精确真实验证与完整性不可兼得

entities.name: 校准
entities.explain: 预测模型的概率输出需要与实际结果频率一致，即预测为70%的事件应实际发生70%

entities.name: 真实验证
entities.explain: 一种校准度量，要求预测者无法通过虚假报告来获得更好的评分

cards.summary: 研究者解决了Haghtalab等人提出的开放问题，证明在顺序二元预测中，精确真实验证与完整性和可靠性不相容。这意味着无法设计一个既完全诚实又完整的校准度量。该结果为在线预测和机器学习中的校准理论提供了重要的负面结果。
cards.relevant: 该理论结果对在线预测系统的设计和评估有重要影响，为理解校准度量的局限性提供了关键见解。

A calibration measure assigns numerical error to miscalibrated reports. Haghtalab et al. (2024) proposed an approximately truthful calibration measure for online prediction, leaving open whether exact truthfulness is compatible with completeness and soundness. We resolve this question negatively for sequential binary prediction: exact truthfulness is incompatible with completeness

entities.explain: 一个包含60种心理治疗干预措施的清单，用于分类治疗师的行为

entities.name: 本体论
entities.explain: 一种对概念进行分类和组织的系统，这里指对治疗动作的分类体系

cards.summary: 研究者引入了一个包含十种治疗动作的本体论，基于MULTI-60清单，通过五名持证心理学家的标注活动验证，并使用法官方法扩展。将该本体论应用于真实咨询记录和模型主导的会话，研究者发现LLM在心理治疗中的行为模式与人类治疗师存在差异，为理解和改进AI心理支持提供了工具。
cards.relevant: 随着越来越多用户向LLM寻求情感支持，该研究为评估和改善AI心理治疗的质量提供了重要框架。

entities.name: 链式思维

entities.name: 上下文-生成替代定律
entities.explain: 该研究提出的原理，认为显式推理上下文可以替代部分解码时的生成

cards.summary: 该研究提出记忆增强链式思维（Memory-Augmented CoT）方法，通过形式化上下文-生成替代定律，在压缩推理链的同时保持逻辑连贯性。该方法利用记忆机制存储关键推理步骤，减少解码时的生成长度，从而降低推理开销，同时保持任务性能。
cards.relevant: 该方法解决了LLM推理成本高的问题，为在资源受限环境中部署复杂推理模型提供了实用方案。

items.title: OmniAssistBench: Assistant-style Interaction Benchmark for Omni-LLMs
items.summary: Recent omni-modal large language models (Omni-LLMs) show great potential as real-time video assistants, which continuously perceive environments and guide users to achieve specific goals. Unlike traditional passive video understanding, interactive assistants should actively combine visual states, user goals, and prior knowledge to provide effective help. Evaluating this is rather challenging, as the model's unpredictable response dynamically changes the user's subsequent actions, which static offline datasets cannot accommodate. To address this bottleneck, we introduce OmniAssistBench. To solve the issue of diverging interaction paths where the same user goal can be achieved through various methods, we provide models with predefined priors derived from the source video, requiring them to guide users along the exact same routes. Since real interaction videos are rare, we construct the dataset by reverse-engineering existing Internet videos. We deduce logical user goals and segment the videos into multi-turn clips to simulate continuous interactions. This rigorous pipeline required over 1000 expert person-hours to build the dataset. Results show that the proprietary Gemini-3-Pro reaches 66.4 out of the max point of 100, while the open-source Qwen3-Omni-Instruct achieves 51.2. Although current models generally understand user inputs, they frequently provide incorrect or incomplete answers. items.title: bentt 在「Anthropic's best AI model struggles to a」下的评论
items.summary: They've put themselves in a corner. Fable was too good and they gave it away with the $20 plan. It had to be a big step from Opus 4.8 to show progress, and Opus 4.8 is GREAT at coding in many different domains. But they're getting killed on token cost. They have to get people paying more for tokens. So then they put Fable in the $200 plan and release Opus 5. I'm suspicious of Opus 5. It is mostly worse than 4.8. It _seems_ like they nerfed it to create more distance between it and Fable. So what have most of us done? Stayed on Opus 4.8. The statistics bear this out. 4.8 still dominates. Now they're stuck. If they take 4.8 away, everyone will riot. If they make Opus 5.x better than 4.8, they disincentivize everyone from moving to Fable and most importantly, paying more. Really, all they can do is take the L for now and just let 4.8 be the apex of the $20 pro plan for the foreseeable future while they work like hell to make Fable THAT much better that it earns the $200 to $infinity that they really want everyone to pay.

items.title: YuechenLi 在「My agent.md to improve LLM-assisted code」下的评论
items.summary:
Since we are sharing our AGENTS.md, I thought I'd share my own, because most of the time, this is pretty much all you need for LLMs to write good code, everything else can be added per project:
----
*Convergence rule*
Every substantial task must end in exactly one of three states: A. Success
The intended capability works in the real path and the real motivating case materially improves. B. Meaningful progression
The capability is not complete, but one genuine blocker is removed and the next blocker is isolated with evidence. C. Honest stop
Further work would require overbroad scope expansion, excessive debt, brittle patching, or tangled logic. Stop and report the reason with concrete evidence. Do not continue producing patches once the work stops converging. Do not confuse activity with progress. A failed attempt is only acceptable if it leaves behind a narrower problem, stronger evidence, or a justified stop. Any partial work must leave the codebase in a cleaner, more legible, and more diagnosable state than before.
---- A lot of the article's AGENTS.md just feel like telling the LLM agents either something they already know (for example, most of the time they know to use exhaustive switch/match statements instead of "arrow anti-pattern") or seems actively harmful ("keep function names short" seems arbitrary and may cause the LLMs to write weird abbreviations for functions that are harder to read and review.
items.author: YuechenLi

items.title: Supermancho 在「My agent.md to improve LLM-assisted code」下的评论
items.summary: It's interesting to read these things. I would describe this as 13 code writing rules (interpreted to be at least 16 - Starting with reduce code indentation) plus a commit message instruction set which I chose to ignore - because it's style-specific and not interesting to me. 8 or 9 of these rules are not necessary. Basic CS is not something I have needed to ask agents, I use, to follow. eg Explaining that you need explicit interfaces is not a necessary instruction, nor is leveraging early return. Unclear instructions are of limited utility. What "Let the reader of the code breathe" or "reduce code indentation" means is subjective and will rarely be effective. Maybe the training for the language being used has gaps, which others do not. If you want to measure, ask it to output a string when it applies a rule. You'll figure out what works, what doesn't and how often, quickly. There's 3 or 4 style choices included. The rest are not something I would use, but we all get burned by different things so I get it.
items.author: Supermancho

items.summary: Smells like „product engineering“. So a product or an engineering lead gets a task to reduce risks of specific abuse by preventing someone from sending email from yahoo or web.de clone. As a quick solution they add this filter without „overthinking“ it. The impact is low, a few customers in a million, so its stupidity gets unnoticed and, once first complaint reaches them, quietly deprioritized to death. Removing it is cheap: the justification for taking that work is likely the show stopper. Google is an old large corp that hires and fires at a scale. Owning removal of abuse filter to increase revenue by Planck-sized amount is an impossible thing.

items.summary: > Just for context, this is a premium domain with a very high premium renewal fee, no history of abuse obviously. The registry premium domains on the new TLDs have several issues.  The biggest IMO is a lack of price protection.  Non-premium domains at least get the cohort based protection from section 2.10c of the registry agreement. So, in addition to being treated as a 2nd rate domain, there’s nothing stopping the registry from cranking up the price if a domain gets popular.  I don’t think it’s ever happened, but have never found contractual terms that forbid it. I made a website about it a while ago after a registry reclassified one of my domains from standard to premium.  https://tldrisk.com/beyond-basics/premium-domains/
